reason: Section 19.01 contains distinct first-election topics: election law and Order in Council priority, candidate residence and ward candidacy, ward voting and ballots, and election notice and voters lists.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal Elections Act application, polling divisions and Order in Council priority for first elections
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19.01(1), 19.01(2) and 19.01(8) address Municipal Elections Act application, revised polling divisions and conflicts with an Order in Council.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Municipal Elections Act, polling divisions and Order in Council provisions apply to first elections.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Candidate residence qualifications for first elections and ward councillor candidacy
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19.01(3) and 19.01(4.01) set residence requirements for mayor or councillor candidates and additional ward residence at nomination.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the residence qualifications for first-election candidates and ward councillor candidates.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ward voting and ballot papers in first elections
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19.01(4.1) and 19.01(4.2) address ward voting, separate ballot papers and the exception for mayor or councillor-at-large candidates.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how ward voting and ballot papers work in a first election for a ward-divided municipality.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice of Election and voters lists for first elections
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19.01(5) to 19.01(7) cover Notice of Election and the preliminary or new voters list for first elections.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Notice of Election and voters-list rules for first elections.

reason: Section 19.02 is a single borrowing-transition rule allowing outstanding borrowing authority of a former municipality to continue in the new municipality with written Minister authorization.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuation of former municipal borrowing authority after amalgamation

evidenceText: outstanding authority of a former municipality to borrow money

proposedGroups.reason: The target states how approved borrowing authority may continue after an amalgamation order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when outstanding borrowing authority of a former municipality may continue in the name of the new municipality.

reason: Section 19.1 separates designation of planning instruments for a newly incorporated municipality from the new council’s review duty and the continued force of deemed instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Designated planning instruments deemed by-laws of newly incorporated municipality
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19.1(1) and 19.1(2) deem designated rural plans or Community Planning Act regulations to be the municipality’s planning instruments or by-laws as of incorporation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how designated planning instruments are deemed valid municipal instruments when unincorporated areas become a new municipality.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Review and continued force of deemed planning instruments
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19.1(3) and 19.1(4) require a five-year review and report to the Minister and keep deemed instruments in force until repealed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the review duty and continued force of planning instruments deemed under section 19.1.

reason: Section 19.2 separates deemed planning instruments for annexed areas and zoning-conflict priority from the annexing council’s review and amendment duty and continued-force rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Planning instruments deemed for annexed areas and zoning conflict priority
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19.2(1) to 19.2(3) deem designated instruments or prior zoning to apply in annexed areas and state that deemed zoning prevails over a conflicting municipal plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how planning and zoning instruments are deemed for annexed areas and what prevails in a municipal plan conflict.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Review, amendment and continued force after annexation
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19.2(4) and 19.2(5) require review and amendment within one and one-half years and keep deemed instruments in force until repealed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the annexing council’s review and amendment duty and the continued force of deemed planning instruments.

reason: Section 19.3 is one application rule extending sections 19.1 and 19.2 to rural communities with necessary modifications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application of planning-instrument transition rules to rural communities
proposedGroups.reason: The target applies two specified planning transition sections to rural communities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that sections 19.1 and 19.2 apply with necessary modifications to rural communities.

reason: Section 20 is a coherent by-law continuity rule for former municipalities after incorporation changes, amalgamation, annexation and decrement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuity or extension of former municipal by-laws after structural changes
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address which by-laws remain in force, extend to an annexed area or apply to a decreased municipality after structural changes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how by-laws continue, extend or apply after incorporation changes, amalgamation, annexation or decreased territorial limits.

reason: Section 21 is one assets-and-liabilities continuity rule for new municipalities and decreased territorial limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assets and liabilities after municipal structural changes
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address how assets and liabilities transfer to a new municipality or are adjusted when territorial limits decrease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how assets and liabilities of former municipalities and local commissions are treated after incorporation, amalgamation or decreased limits.

reason: Section 22 separates rescission and deemed village status for local improvement districts and named communities from the powers, services, assets and liabilities of the resulting villages.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rescission and deemed village status for local improvement districts and named communities
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 22(1) to 22(3.1) rescind incorporations, deem named entities to be villages and continue those villages until changed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which incorporations are rescinded and how the affected entities are deemed and continued as villages.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Powers, services, assets and liabilities of villages created under subsection 22(3)
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 22(4) addresses the powers and services the created village may carry out and the transfer of assets and liabilities from former entities within it.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what powers, services, assets and liabilities pass to a village created under subsection 22(3).

reason: Section 23 is one historical establishment power allowing Cabinet to establish an area outside municipal limits as a local service district for a service being provided there on November 9, 1966.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local service district establishment for pre-existing outside-municipality services

evidenceText: outside the territorial limits of a municipality
establish the area as a local service district

proposedGroups.reason: The target states when an outside-municipality area with an existing service may be established as a local service district.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an area outside municipal limits may be established as a local service district under section 23.

reason: Section 23.01 is a definitions provision defining service for sections 23.1 to 27.01, including certain recreational or community facilities and excluding gas sale and customer services.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service definition for local service district provisions
proposedGroups.reason: The target defines service for sections 23.1 to 27.01.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definition of service for sections 23.1 to 27.01.

reason: Section 23.1 is a focused regulation power defining local service district boundaries or areas and prescribing services, with a special rule for garbage and refuse collection and disposal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations defining local service district boundaries and prescribed services
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address regulations that define local service district boundaries or areas and prescribe services, including garbage service under section 191 regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation power for local service district boundaries and services, including garbage and refuse collection and disposal.

reason: Section 24 is too broad for one unit because it covers creating a local service district, meeting quorum and voting, repeat-petition and adjournment rules, later boundary changes or amalgamations, grouped annexations, service continuity and elector qualification dates.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Petition or Minister-initiated meeting to establish a local service district
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 24(1) to 24(4) set the petition or Minister-initiated process, boundary definition, meeting call, attendance threshold, majority decision, establishment power, one-year petition bar and adjournment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the petition, meeting, quorum, majority, one-year bar and adjournment rules for establishing a local service district.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Adding areas, annexing, amalgamating or changing local service district boundaries
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 24(5) to 24(6.2) address meetings for additions, annexations, amalgamations, boundary changes and grouped contiguous areas.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how local service district areas may be added, annexed, amalgamated or changed, including grouped-area contiguity.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service continuity and elector qualification date after local service district changes
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 24(7) and 24(8) state that existing services continue after boundary changes unless discontinued and set the qualification date for electors.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how services continue after local service district boundary changes and which date determines elector qualifications.
